([[Chatsworth, Los Angeles|Chatsworth, California]]) | college = [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] (2019–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team1 = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team2 = →[[South Bay Lakers]] | years3 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team3 = South Bay Lakers | years4 = {{nbay|2023|end}}–present | team4 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | highlights = * [[NBA G League]] Next Up Game ([[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]]) * 2× First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2021, 2022) * SEC All-Freshman Team (2020) }} '''Scotty Maurice Pippen Jr.''' (born November 10, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]], where he earned [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman Team recognition in 2020 and First-team All-conference recognition in 2021 and 2022. ==Early life== Pippen was born in [[Portland, Oregon]], while his father, future [[Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall-of-Fame]] [[small forward]] [[Scottie Pippen]], was playing for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Scotty Pippen Jr. powers Sierra Canyon past Jefferson for spot in LSI title game|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/highschoolsports/2018/12/scotty-pippen-jr-powers-sierra-canyon-past-jefferson-for-spot-in-lsi-title-game.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=December 29, 2018}} From kindergarten to tenth grade, Scotty attended [[Pine Crest School]] in Florida.{{cite web |title=Scotty Pippen Jr. & Kenyon Martin Jr. Are Hooping at Sierra Canyon HS |url=https://slamonline.com/college-hs/scotty-pippen-jr-kenyon-martin-jr-are-hooping-at-sierra-canyon-hs/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|SLAM]] |publisher=[[Slam (magazine)|SLAM Media Inc.]] |access-date=21 February 2026}} Before his junior year, his family moved to the L.A. area, and he transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles|Chatsworth, California]], which had a more competitive basketball team. At Sierra, he played alongside future NBA players such as [[Marvin Bagley III]], [[Kenyon Martin Jr.]], and [[Cassius Stanley]].{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=Next generation NBA royalty packs Sierra Canyon roster|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/sierra-canyon-scottie-pippen-kenyon-martin-derek-fisher-cassius-stanley-duane-washington-terren-frank-sons-nephew-nba-royalty|work=USA Today High School Sports|date=December 18, 2017|access-date=January 15, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 16.3 points, 4.6 assists, and 3.6 rebounds per game and helped his team win the [[California Interscholastic Federation]] Open Division state title.{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Young|title=Jerry Stackhouse signs Scottie Pippen's son as first recruit at Vanderbilt|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/jerry-stackhouse-signs-scottie-pippen-son-first-recruit-vanderbilt-042506813.html|work=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=April 26, 2019|access-date=January 15, 2021}} Pippen competed for the Oakland Soldiers on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=Peach Jam: Scotty Pippen Jr. faces unreal pressure and he loves it|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/peach-jam-scotty-pippen-jr-faces-unreal-pressure-and-he-loves-it-scottie-pippen|work=USA Today High School Sports|date=July 12, 2018|access-date=January 15, 2021}} He committed to a future playing college basketball for [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] over offers from [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco]], [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]], and [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]].{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Boone|title=College basketball recruiting: Son of Hall of Famer Scottie Pippen commits to Vanderbilt|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-recruiting-son-of-hall-of-famer-scottie-pippen-commits-to-vanderbilt/|website=CBSSports.com|date=January 11, 2019|access-date=January 15, 2021}}{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Scotty Pippen Jr., son of Hall of Famer, commits to Vanderbilt|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25738527/scotty-pippen-jr-4-star-recruit-commits-vanderbilt-commodores|work=[[ESPN]]|date=January 11, 2019|access-date=January 15, 2021}} ==College career== On November 20, 2019, Pippen scored a freshman season-high 21 points in a 90–72 win over [[Austin Peay Governors basketball|Austin Peay]].{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Sparks|title=Vanderbilt basketball: Scotty Pippen Jr.'s big night nets win over Austin Peay|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2019/11/20/live-updates-vanderbilt-basketball-austin-peay-aaron-nesmith-saben-lee-jerry-stackhouse/4225812002/|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=November 20, 2019|access-date=January 15, 2021}} In his regular season finale on March 7, 2020, he scored 21 points for a second time in an 83–74 victory over [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite web|title=Vanderbilt tops South Carolina 83-74 behind Pippen in finale|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166387|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 7, 2020|access-date=January 15, 2021}} As a freshman, Pippen averaged 12 points and 3.6 rebounds per game, earning [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite news|first=Robbie|last=Weinstei|title=Vanderbilt's Saben Lee, Scotty Pippen Jr. earn All-SEC honors|url=https://247sports.com/college/vanderbilt/Article/Vanderbilt-Commodores-Saben-Lee-Scotty-Pippen-Jr-earn-All-SEC-honors-144836673/|work=247 Sports|date=March 10, 2020|access-date=March 26, 2020}} The impending departures of future NBA players [[Aaron Nesmith]] and [[Saben Lee]] led to a future expectation of a leading role on the team, which came to fruition in his sophomore season.{{cite web|first=Gentry|last=Estes|title=Vanderbilt basketball's Scotty Pippen Jr. has unfinished business with Kentucky|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2021/01/06/vanderbilt-basketball-scotty-pippen-jr-kentucky/4119111001/|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=January 6, 2021|access-date=January 15, 2021}} On December 27, 2020, Pippen scored 30 points in an 87–50 win over [[Alcorn State Braves basketball|Alcorn State]].{{cite web|first=Kris|last=Rhim|title=Vanderbilt 87, Alcorn State 50: Scotty Pippen Jr. scores career-high 30 points|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2020/12/27/vanderbilt-basketball-beats-alcorn-state-scotty-pippen-jr-scores-30-points/3956599001/|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=December 27, 2020|access-date=January 15, 2021}} On January 9, 2021, he recorded his first [[double-double]], with 18 points and 12 assists in an 84–81 loss to [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]].{{cite web|title=Molinar, Stewart help Bulldogs hold off Vanderbilt 84-81|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401258739|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 9, 2021|access-date=January 15, 2021}} On January 27, 2021, Pippen scored 32 points in a 78–71 loss to [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite web|first=Drake|last=Hills|title=Scotty Pippen Jr. scores career-high 32 points but Vanderbilt basketball falls to Florida|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2021/01/27/vanderbilt-basketball-scotty-pippen-jr-career-high-florida-sec/6680033002/|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=January 27, 2021|access-date=January 29, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 20.8 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game. On April 10, 2021, Pippen declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his future college eligibility.{{cite web|first=Wilton|last=Jackson|title=Vanderbilt Guard Scotty Pippen Jr Declares for 2021 NBA Draft|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2021/04/10/vanderbilt-guard-scotty-pippen-jr-declares-for-nba-draf|website=SI.com|date=April 10, 2021|access-date=May 10, 2021}}{{Dead link|date=November 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} He later withdrew from the draft returning to Vanderbilt for his junior season. On December 7, 2021, Pippen made a last second three-pointer to tie the game against [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]]. As a junior, he averaged 20.4 points, 4.5 assists, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.9 steals per game. He was named to the First Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] as a junior.{{cite press release|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|website=SECSports.com|publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]]|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2022}} That season, he led the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] in scoring.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/justin-pippen-scottie-pippens-youngest-son-commits-to-michigan-203650705.html|title=Justin Pippen, Scottie Pippen's youngest son, commits to Michigan|accessdate=December 18, 2025|date=April 19, 2024|work=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|author=Peek, Krysten}} On April 18, 2022, Pippen declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining future college eligibility.{{cite web|first=Torrence|last=Banks|title=Scotty Pippen Jr. declares for 2022 NBA Draft|url=https://www.wsmv.com/2022/04/18/scotty-pippen-jr-declares-2022-nba-draft/|website=WSMV.com|access-date=April 18, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2022–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Pippen signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on July 1, 2022, splitting time with their G-League affiliate, the [[South Bay Lakers]],{{cite web|title=Lakers sign Scotty Pippen Jr. and Cole Swider to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-scotty-pippen-jr-and-cole-swider-to-two-way-contracts-220701?amp=1|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2022|access-date=July 1, 2022}} subsequently joining Los Angeles for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612747/lakers|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 21, 2022}} In his Summer League debut, Pippen scored 14 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists, and a block in a 100–66 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Miami Heat Jul 2, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/lal-vs-mia-1322200001/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 21, 2022}} He was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.{{cite web|title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}} On September 7, 2023, Pippen re-signed with the Lakers on an Exhibit 10 contract,{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-four-players-090723|website=NBA.com|date=September 7, 2023|access-date=September 8, 2023}} but was waived on October 16.{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Waive Three Players|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-waive-three-players-10-16-23|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}} ===South Bay Lakers (2023–2024)=== On October 28, 2023, Pippen rejoined the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Finalize Training Camp Roster and Schedule|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-finalize-2324-training-camp-roster-and-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2024–present)=== On January 16, 2024, Pippen signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite tweet|author=Grizzlies PR|title=The @memgrizz today announced the team signed Scotty Pippen Jr. to a two-way contract.|number=1747357190548009281|user=GrizzliesPR|date=January 16, 2024|access-date=January 16, 2024}} On October 15, Pippen's contract was converted to a standard four–year contract.{{cite web|title=GRIZZLIES SIGN SCOTTY PIPPEN JR. TO MULTI-YEAR CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-scotty-pippen-jr-to-multi-year-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2024|access-date=October 17, 2024}} On November 2, 2024, Pippen recorded 12 points and a career-high 13 assists in a 124–107 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-roll-past-76ers-124-107|title=Grizzlies Roll Past 76ers, 124-107|website=nba.com|date=November 3, 2024|access-date=November 4, 2024}} On November 8, Pippen recorded his first career triple-double with 11 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 128–104 win over the [[Washington Wizards]]. He and his father, [[Scottie Pippen|Scottie]], became the first [[List of second-generation NBA players|father-son duo]] in NBA history to each record a triple-double.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/grizzlies-news-scotty-pippen-jr-never-before-seen-history-father-scottie-pippen|title=Grizzlies' Scotty Pippen Jr. makes never-before-seen history with father Scottie Pippen|website=ClutchPoints|last=Giuliano|first=Sonny|date=November 9, 2024|access-date=November 10, 2024}} On November 23, Pippen recorded a career-high 30 points along with 10 assists in a 142–131 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/grizzlies-news-scotty-pippen-jr-dads-kill-message-playing-bulls|title=Grizzlies' Scotty Pippen Jr. reveals dad's 'kill' message about playing Bulls|website=ClutchPoints|last=Crisafulli|first=Owen|date=November 24, 2024|access-date=November 24, 2024}} He made 79 appearances (21 starts) for Memphis during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 9.9 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 4.4 assists. On April 20, 2025, Pippen made his playoff debut in the first round of the NBA playoffs, recording two points and four assists in a 131–80 Game 1 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |title=Thunder beat Grizzlies 131-80 in Game 1, 5th-biggest margin of victory in NBA postseason history |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401767818 |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=ESPN}} On April 24, he had a team-high 28 points, alongside five rebounds, five assists and three steals, in a 114–108 Game 3 loss.{{Cite web |title=Thunder rally from 29 points down after Morant leaves with injury, top Grizzlies for 3-0 series lead |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401767904 |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} On April 26, Pippen had a team-high 30 points, alongside 11 rebounds and four assists, in a 117–115 Game 4 loss, eliminating the Grizzlies from the playoffs.{{Cite web |title=Thunder complete sweep of Grizzlies, reach Western Conference semifinals with 117-115 victory |url=https://www.nba.com/game/okc-vs-mem-0042400144 |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=NBA}} On October 18, 2025, it was announced that Pippen would miss at least 12 weeks after undergoing a [[sesamoid bone|sesamoidectomy]] to address a lingering left big toe injury.{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2025-10-18 |title=Sources: Grizzlies' Scotty Pippen Jr. out at least 12 weeks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46638143/sources-grizzlies-scotty-pippen-jr-least-12-weeks |access-date=2026-02-24 |website=ESPN.com}} On February 6, 2026, Pippen made his season debut, recording 13 points, three rebounds, and six assists in a 115-135 loss to the [[2025–26 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' Scotty Pippen: Starting in 2025-26 debut|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-scotty-pippen-starting-in-2025-26-debut/|access-date=March 4, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On February 21, Pippen was involved in an altercation with [[Myron Gardner]] during a 120–136 loss to the [[2025–26 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]], one which resulted in both of their ejections; the pair were ultimately fined $35,000 each for the incident.{{Cite web|title=Scotty Pippen Jr., Myron Gardner fined $35,000 each for Grizzlies-Heat scuffle|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48015578/scotty-pippen-jr-myron-gardner-fined-35000-grizzlies-heat-scuffle|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He would appear in 10 games (including six starts) for Memphis during the regular season, averaging 11.4 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 4.7 assists. On March 13, Pippen was ruled out for the remainder of the season after undergoing another sesamoidectomy procedure.{{cite web |title=Scotty Pippen Jr. to miss rest of season |url=https://basketnews.com/news-243003-scotty-pippen-jr-to-miss-rest-of-season.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=15 April 2026 |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2022}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A. .343 || .763 || 3.1 || 4.3 || 1.6 || .2 || 17.5 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Pippen is the son of [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] basketball player [[Scottie Pippen]], who won six NBA championships with the [[Chicago Bulls]] during his 17-year career in the league,{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Arias|title=Vanderbilt's Pippen Jr. Sharing Spotlight with Famous Father|url=https://www.si.com/college/vanderbilt/basketball/vanderbilts-pippen-jr-sharing-spotlight-with-famous-father|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=April 21, 2020|access-date=January 15, 2021}} and media personality [[Larsa Pippen]], a cast member on ''[[The Real Housewives of Miami]]''. His mother is of [[Assyrian people|Assyrian]] descent. He is the cousin of [[Kavion Pippen]] who is an American professional [[basketball]] player.{{cite web|title=Scotty Pippen Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/pippesc01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|access-date=July 8, 2022}} His younger brother, [[Justin Pippen]], played for the [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2024–25 Michigan Wolverines]] basketball team before transferring to play for [[California Golden Bears men's basketball]]. == See also == * [[List of second-generation NBA players]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://vucommodores.com/roster/scotty-pippen-jr/ Vanderbilt Commodores bio] *{{commons category-inline}} {{Memphis Grizzlies current roster}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Pippen, Scotty Jr.}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:American people of Assyrian descent]] [[Category:American people of Lebanese descent]] [[Category:American people of Syrian descent]] [[Category:Assyrian sportspeople]] [[Category:Basketball players from Portland, Oregon]] [[Category:Los Angeles Lakers players]] [[Category:Memphis Grizzlies players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sierra Canyon School alumni]] [[Category:South Bay Lakers players]] [[Category:Sportspeople of Syrian descent]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball players]]
